conventions.convention: Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences. The category is a complex modular ribbon fusion category; modularity means invertibility of the Hopf-link matrix, without positivity or unitarity assumptions.
Choose either nonzero square root D of the sum of squared pivotal dimensions; S=s/D, p₊=Σᵢθᵢdᵢ², and κ=p₊/D. Dimension formulas contain no complex conjugation.
Composition uses individual bordism homology relations and the middle-surface Walker correction μ(R₁λ₀,λ₁,R₂ᵗλ₂). Increasing the integer weight by one multiplies the assigned map by κ.

For the torus, ω(m,l)=1 and α=λ=ℝm; matrix columns are images of m,l. The positive Hopf class is [[0,1],[-1,0]], the positive core twist is [[1,1],[0,1]], and their operators obey S²=C and (ST)³=κI. The inverse Hopf class instead obeys (S⁻¹T)³=κC.
The SU(2) example assumes integer k≥1, ℓ=k+2, q=exp(πi/ℓ), and the actual positive-trace Lusztig tilting ribbon quotient, with labels 0 through k.

load_bearing.statement: The weighted RT model is this category, these finite-dimensional complex state spaces, and the exact surgery-defined symmetric monoidal functor Z of the supplied theorem. It includes actual coupon morphisms, disconnected bordisms and empty ends; increasing an integer weight by one multiplies the map by κ.

Under full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences, for the specified complex modular ribbon fusion category and weighted RT model, dim V(Σ_g)=ΣᵢS₀ᵢ^(2−2g) for every integer g≥0, without complex conjugation. The sphere dimension is one and the unmarked torus dimension is |I|. Every compatible separating or nonseparating cut has the actual normalized tube-sewing isomorphism and complete cutting inverse, retaining multiplicities and specified geometric data.
